title: THE REFEREE WHO LET THEM WIN BY TURNS
deck: For fifty years the water of two moon colonies has hung on a ritual race, and its dying referee has quietly bent every close finish so that neither side wins twice running. Illuminara has nine days to find out what the bend really was, and to help two angry peoples decide, in daylight, what to put in its place.
shape: Six scenes across nine days: a confession offered, a constant hidden in the record, a rehearsal that makes the truth less kind, an open arena and an uproar, a week of counted argument with an audit, and a finish settled by a printed rule.

scenes.title: The Chair
paragraphs: *Kessel Arena, referee's box · nine days before the Carry, 06:40*

Ketterly Osa had called the Long Carry for forty-nine years from a chair bolted to the box floor, and for the last four she had needed an oxygen line to reach it. Illuminara found her there before the ice crews arrived, fitting a new cannula with the unhurried fingers of a woman threading a needle.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Sit. You are the neutral witness, so be neutral at me for a minute. I have something to confess, and I want to choose the room.

**Illuminara**  
Whenever you like.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Every close finish I have ever called, I called so that neither colony won twice running. Harrow took three in a row in my second year. Vesper shut the Ice Line valve for forty days, and a clinic on the north ring lost its pumps. I swore I would never call a third.

Thirteen thousand empty seats rose around them in the low gravity, ticking as the ice cooled. Illuminara felt the quick, kind sentence rise in her, *it isn't fraud*, and did not say it. She had not earned it yet. A sentence that comforts before it is checked is only a nicer way of not listening.

**Illuminara**  
Have you written the calls down anywhere?

**Ketterly Osa**  
A cheat's diary? No.

**Illuminara**  
Then the races kept it for you. The photo-strips are public.

**Ketterly Osa**  
If I say it aloud, Pavo Reisz will say fifty years of Harrow's water came out of a fraud, and he will be right to. Vesper will hear that every win they cheered was a present. They will both walk out and the valve will shut. I am not afraid of dying, witness. I am afraid of dying on top of that.

**Illuminara**  
Give me three of the nine days before you say a word to anyone.
Ketterly looked at her over the tube for a long moment. *She is deciding whether I am kind or only curious,* Illuminara thought, and could not have said which answer was true.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Three. After that I speak, and you can hold my coat.

scenes.title: The Width of a Kindness
paragraphs: *Race archive, sub-level two · day two, 21:15*

A cheat's record wanders. A bribe has the size of the bribe, a grudge the size of the grudge. Illuminara pinned the fifty photo-strips along the archive wall and measured, for each of the nineteen finishes the camera could not honestly split, the distance between where the line had really fallen and where Ketterly had put it. She expected scatter. She got a staircase.

**Illuminara**  
Your bends are not the size of a mood. For eleven years they are flat, three or four tenths of a second, the size of a kindness. Then they start to climb, a little every year, like a tree ring, until last year's is eight-tenths. A kindness has no growth curve. Something else does.

**Ketterly Osa**  
I only ever felt the finishes were wrong. I took the wrongness for my own.
So she went looking for whatever else had grown for fifty years, and found it in the Accord's ninth section, in a table nobody read aloud because everybody believed they knew it.

**Illuminara**  
The Allowance Table. Vesper is credited four-tenths of a second at the line for every thousand hearths it trails Harrow. The table was struck in 2061, when the gap was one thousand. It still says one thousand. By the census, the gap is three.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Then the fair credit is a second and two-tenths, and the table gives them four-tenths.

**Illuminara**  
And the rule has handed Harrow the difference at every close finish, a little more each year. Nothing Harrow's skaters did. The letter of the rule did it, and you stood in front of it with your wrist.
Ketterly laughed, which turned into coughing, which Illuminara waited out with the cup held ready and no advice.

**Ketterly Osa**  
So I was never cheating them at all.

**Illuminara**  
Not for the last thirty-eight years. For the first eleven you were, because the gap was too small to explain a bend that wide. Those were mercy, and they were yours. You did two different things under one name.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Do not make me innocent, witness. A little guilty I can carry. All guilty I could bear. Innocent I would have to explain.

**Illuminara**  
I am not making you anything. Pavo will be right about the first eleven years.

Illuminara found she was smiling at a dying woman who had matched a statute with her forearm, and put the smile away. It was not what the room needed. She kept the wonder underneath it, where it warmed her anyway.

**Illuminara**  
One condition. I will not hand this over as your defence. If I do, they will hear a lawyer, and they will be right to. You tell them first, in your own words. The number comes second, as something they can check.

scenes.title: Make It True
paragraphs: *Referee's box · day three, 23:50*

They rehearsed until the arena lights went to night-blue. Illuminara did not write the speech. She propped the pillow behind Ketterly's back, kept the oxygen line out of the way of her elbow, and listened to the confession arrive in softer and softer versions.

**Ketterly Osa**  
For a period of years, in the interest of order, I exercised a degree of latitude in my calls.

**Illuminara**  
Say it as if Pavo were the one in this chair.

**Ketterly Osa**  
I cheated Harrow for eleven years because I was frightened.
The cannula hissed. Ketterly pressed her palm flat on the chair arm, as if to hold the sentence down.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Better. Worse. Which is it?

**Illuminara**  
I think it is the first true thing you have said tonight.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Make it kind, then. They need something to forgive me with.

**Illuminara**  
Kind is what you did. They never got to choose it. Let it be true and let them decide how kind to be.

At two in the morning Ketterly asked her to say the arithmetic first, to stand in front of her with it. Illuminara said no, as gently as she had ever said anything, and sat with her through the rest of the night instead. When the coughing took Ketterly the second time she held the cup and said nothing. It was not a solution. It was the only thing in the building that was needed.

**Ketterly Osa**  
You know both of them will want my chair when I'm gone.

**Illuminara**  
Then we should leave them something better than a chair to fight over.

scenes.title: Daylight
paragraphs: *Kessel Arena, the open Calling of the Rule · day four, 14:00*

The Calling was an old custom: once a year the whole arena heard the Accord read aloud, so that nobody could say they had not known the rule. Thirteen thousand people sat in it, and the two delegations faced each other in boxes on the ice. Ketterly spoke last, from her chair, from the line she had called for forty-nine years.

**Ketterly Osa**  
For forty-nine years I have decided close finishes so that neither colony won twice running. For the first eleven I did it out of fear, and I took finishes from Harrow that were Harrow's. The nineteen are on the wall in the concourse, with the year and the margin. I am not going to tell you it was kind.

The noise began low, like water finding a drain. A flask came spinning down from the third tier toward the chair. Illuminara was between it and Ketterly before most of the arena had seen it leave a hand. She caught it, set it on the ice, and said nothing, because that was all the strength the moment required.

**Pavo Reisz**  
If it was a lie, then fifty years of our water came from a fraud, and I will not sit in an arena that was built on it.

**Maren Tsoi**  
She gave us our wins. Say it plainly, Pavo. You would call that a theft, and we would not.

**Teodor Brask**  
Year six. Anchor leg. Ansel Brask crossed first by three-tenths. My grandfather.

**Ketterly Osa**  
He did. I gave it to Vesper. That one I did to him.

**Teodor Brask**  
He never skated again.

**Ketterly Osa**  
I know.
She did not add a reason. In the quiet that followed, the young man's anger stayed exactly where it was, and Illuminara noticed that Ketterly let it.

**Illuminara**  
I have one thing to add, and I am asking you not to believe it. There is a table in the Accord that has not been updated since 2061. By my count it has handed close finishes to Harrow for decades, and by my count Ketterly's bends tracked it. That is a number, not a defence. The archive, the strips and the census are open from tonight.

**Pavo Reisz**  
And who audits you?

**Illuminara**  
Your engineers. Mine will sit behind them.

**Pavo Reisz**  
I may not sit in the Carry at all.

**Illuminara**  
Then sit in the audit instead. It is a smaller room, and the water depends on it as much.

scenes.title: The Count
paragraphs: *Annex Hall B · day seven, 20:30*
Harrow's engineers had found the table in four hours and her error in six. They put both on the board without ceremony.

**Pavo Reisz**  
You counted every registered hearth. Two hundred and fifty on our side are cold. Nobody has lived in them since the second winter. The true gap is two thousand seven hundred and fifty, not three thousand. Your drift is seven-tenths, not eight.

**Illuminara**  
Seven. Thank you. I'll strike it from my sheet and sign yours.
She did, in front of the room. It changed the number by a tenth of a second and the room by a good deal more.

Then the engineers did what she had asked of them and nothing she hadn't. Harrow's team and Vesper's team each chose three years she had never shown them, fourteen, twenty-nine and forty-four, and pulled Ketterly's recorded bend and that year's census gap without seeing each other's work until it reached the board. In years fourteen and forty-four the bend sat within a tenth of the indexed allowance. Year twenty-nine was the awkward one: Ketterly had bent four-tenths less than the gap predicted, and nobody could say why. They left the residual on the board unexplained.

They also tried the rival explanation, that she had simply alternated winners and the staircase was only coincidence. Alternation would have bent a finish only after one colony had won twice. The bends came in years with no such history, and they grew with the census, whichever colony had won last.

**Pavo Reisz**  
Fine. It's a trend. It doesn't make it honest.

**Illuminara**  
No. It makes it two things. For eleven years she chose a side. For thirty-eight she followed a table that had stopped being true.

Two proposals were on the board by midnight. Harrow's chief engineer wanted the Allowance indexed to the census, recounted every year by both colonies together, no human hand in it. Maren wanted what Ketterly had done by hand, written into the Accord: a printed Turn Credit of three-tenths of a second to whichever colony lost the year before.

**Pavo Reisz**  
That is charity wearing a rule's coat.

**Maren Tsoi**  
It's what we were already living on. This way someone can vote against it.

**Illuminara**  
That is the point. The census mends a fault. The Turn Credit makes a kindness public, and a public kindness can be argued with, shortened, ended. Ketterly's could only be believed or not.

The Accord let each delegation bind its own colony by its own majority, so they voted separately. The census table passed in both delegations without a dissent. The Turn Credit passed Vesper's eight to one and Harrow's five to four, with Pavo among the four. It would lapse at the tenth Carry unless both delegations voted it back, and either colony could decline to renew without penalty or loss of standing. Pavo asked that his no be recorded beside the rule, not beneath it, and it was.

**Teodor Brask**  
I'll skate it. I haven't forgiven her.

**Illuminara**  
Nobody has asked you to.
Then she raised the item no one had put on the board.

**Illuminara**  
The first eleven years are not mine to settle, and not the colonies' either. They belong to the people who lost those finishes.

The two readers who would stand at the line were set to re-read the strips for the eleven. Where the strip, not the hand, showed Harrow first, the Record would be amended in the skater's own name with the date. The skater or the family would choose whether to take the amended result, a season's trim of Vesper's draw credited to their household, both, or neither. Maren said Vesper would pay it to anyone who asked.

**Teodor Brask**  
Put Ansel's name back. Keep the water.
In the gallery, skaters who had won close finishes in the last decade argued in low voices about which of their medals now carried an asterisk. Nobody told them they were wrong to mind.
The water ledger went onto the open board at dawn: every pump log from both colonies, read by both, month by month, from then on.

scenes.title: The Strip
paragraphs: *Kessel Arena, the finish line · day ten, the Carry, 15:20*

The last leg was close enough that thirteen thousand people stopped breathing together. Harrow's anchor crossed first by six-tenths of a second, and by the old letter of the rule that would have been the end of it: Harrow by two-tenths, and a table nobody had read since 2061 doing the calling.

Nobody called it. The strip went up on the board with the new Allowance and the Turn Credit stacked beside it, last year's loser being Harrow, and two readers, one from each box, stood at the line and read it aloud. Maren read the arithmetic. Pavo, because the rule said the losing delegate reads the margin, read the last line, though he had voted against the rule that gave him the line.

**Pavo Reisz**  
Raw finish, Harrow by six-tenths. Indexed allowance to Vesper, one point one. Turn Credit to Harrow, three-tenths. Net: Vesper, by two-tenths.

His voice held. A sound went up from the Vesper stands that was not quite joy, because they knew now what their wins had been made of, and it was the sound of people being handed back something they had always half owned. On the Harrow side nobody threw anything. Teodor Brask, who had skated the second leg clean, stood with his hands on his knees and looked at the board a long time. He did not applaud. He did not leave.

Ketterly watched from the old chair. Nobody had put a flag in her hand. She had the cannula and a cup of tea she was not drinking, and for the first time in forty-nine years she had not had to decide anything.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Eight-tenths, was it?

**Illuminara**  
Seven.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Seven. Corrected by a Harrow engineer, in public. I can die now.

She did, on the Thursday after, in her sleep, with the strip pinned over her bed and the valve open. Pavo Reisz came to the burial and stood at the back. He told Illuminara that he had not forgiven the first eleven years, and that he had come for the other thirty-eight. The chair stayed bolted to the box floor. The next season two people sat in it, one from each colony, and neither could tilt a line.

critic_line: Illuminara learned that Ketterly's secret kindness concealed two different histories: a stolen first eleven years and thirty-eight years of unwitting correction for a frozen rule; by refusing to turn evidence into absolution, she helped both colonies audit the truth, let the harmed choose their own repair and replace one hidden hand with a public rule they could accept, dissent from and later end.

shared_strengths: A strong central idea: hidden mercy turns out to be a stale rule. It has humane dialogue and a satisfying, procedural resolution. The middle section (audit, proposals, votes) gets technical and tidy, and the arithmetic may lose some readers. Still, the emotional beats and the ending land well.

A sharp moral premise, lucid mystery, and humane dialogue create strong momentum. The public correction, unresolved anger, and shared replacement for one person’s mercy are satisfying and memorable. Some readers may find the ethical lessons unusually explicit and the settlement slightly over-neat, but the emotional restraint should carry most through.
shared_reservations: Harrow's engineers had found the table in four hours and her error in six. They put both on the board without ceremony.

translation_sl.title: SODNICA, KI JIM JE PUSTILA ZMAGOVATI IZMENOMA
translation_sl.deck: Voda dveh luninih kolonij je petdeset let visela na obredni tekmi, njena umirajoča sodnica pa je skrivaj ukrivila vsak tesen razplet, da nobena stran ne bi zmagala dvakrat zapored. Illuminara ima devet dni, da ugotovi, kaj je ta odklon v resnici pomenil, in dvema jeznima ljudstvoma pomaga, da se pri belem dnevu odločita, kaj naj ga nadomesti.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v devetih dneh: ponujeno priznanje, konstanta, skrita v evidenci, vaja, zaradi katere je resnica manj prijazna, odprta arena in razburjenje, teden preštetega argumentiranja z revizijo ter cilj, razsojen po natisnjenem pravilu.

scenes.title: Stol
paragraphs: *Arena Kessel, sodniška kabina · devet dni pred Prenosom, 06:40*

Ketterly Osa je devetinštirideset let sodila Dolgi prenos s stola, privitega v tla kabine, zadnja štiri leta pa je za pot do njega potrebovala cevko s kisikom. Illuminara jo je našla tam, še preden so prišle ekipe za led, kako si je z mirnimi prsti ženske, ki vdeva nit v šivanko, nameščala novo nosno kanilo.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Sedi. Ti si nevtralna priča, zato bodi minuto nevtralna do mene. Nekaj moram priznati in želim izbrati prostor.

**Illuminara**  
Ko boš pripravljena.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Vsak tesen razplet, o katerem sem kadar koli odločala, sem razsodila tako, da nobena kolonija ni zmagala dvakrat zapored. Harrow je v mojem drugem letu zmagal trikrat zapored. Vesper je za štirideset dni zaprl ventil Ledene linije in klinika na severnem obroču je ostala brez črpalk. Prisegla sem, da tretje zmage ne bom nikoli dosodila.

Trinajst tisoč praznih sedežev se je dvigalo okoli njiju v nizki težnosti in tiktakalo, ko se je led hladil. Illuminara je začutila, kako se v njej dviga hiter, prijazen stavek, *to ni goljufija*, pa ga ni izrekla. Zanj si še ni prislužila pravice. Stavek, ki tolaži, preden je preverjen, je le prijaznejši način, da ne poslušaš.

**Illuminara**  
Si te odločitve kje zapisovala?

**Ketterly Osa**  
Goljufov dnevnik? Ne.

**Illuminara**  
Potem so jih dirke ohranile namesto tebe. Fototrakovi so javni.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Če to povem naglas, bo Pavo Reisz rekel, da je petdeset let Harrowove vode priteklo iz goljufije, in imel bo prav. Vesper bo slišal, da je bila vsaka zmaga, ki so jo slavili, darilo. Oboji bodo odšli in ventil se bo zaprl. Ne bojim se smrti, priča. Bojim se umreti na vrhu vsega tega.

**Illuminara**  
Daj mi tri od teh devetih dni, preden komur koli kaj poveš.
Ketterly jo je dolgo gledala čez cevko. *Odloča se, ali sem prijazna ali samo radovedna,* je pomislila Illuminara in ne bi znala povedati, kateri odgovor je resničen.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Tri. Potem bom spregovorila, ti pa mi lahko držiš plašč.

scenes.title: Širina dobrote
paragraphs: *Arhiv dirk, druga kletna raven · drugi dan, 21:15*

Goljufov zapis tava. Podkupnina ima velikost podkupnine, zamera velikost zamere. Illuminara je po steni arhiva razporedila petdeset fototrakov in pri vsakem od devetnajstih ciljev, ki jih kamera pošteno ni mogla ločiti, izmerila razdaljo med tem, kje je črta res padla, in kam jo je postavila Ketterly. Pričakovala je raztros. Dobila je stopnišče.

**Illuminara**  
Tvoji odkloni niso veliki kakor razpoloženje. Enajst let so ravni, tri ali štiri desetinke sekunde, velikost dobrote. Nato začnejo naraščati, vsako leto malo, kakor letnice drevesa, dokler lanski ne doseže osmih desetink. Dobrota nima krivulje rasti. Nekaj drugega jo ima.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Vedno sem samo čutila, da so bili razpleti napačni. Mislila sem, da je ta napačnost moja.
Zato je šla iskat, kaj drugega je petdeset let raslo, in našla to v devetem razdelku Sporazuma, v tabeli, ki je nihče ni bral na glas, ker so vsi verjeli, da jo poznajo.

**Illuminara**  
Tabela dodatka. Vesperju na cilju pripadajo štiri desetinke sekunde za vsakih tisoč ognjišč, za kolikor zaostaja za Harrowom. Tabelo so sprejeli leta 2061, ko je bila razlika tisoč. Še vedno piše tisoč. Po popisu je razlika tri tisoč.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Potem je pošteni dodatek sekunda in dve desetinki, tabela pa jim daje štiri desetinke.

**Illuminara**  
In pravilo je pri vsakem tesnem cilju razliko izročilo Harrowu, vsako leto malo več. Nič takega, kar bi naredili Harrowovi drsalci. Naredila je črka pravila, ti pa si ji stopila na pot z zapestjem.
Ketterly se je zasmejala, smeh se je spremenil v kašelj, Illuminara pa je počakala, držeč pripravljeno skodelico in brez nasveta.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Torej jih sploh nikoli nisem goljufala.

**Illuminara**  
Zadnjih osemintrideset let ne. Prvih enajst pa si jih, ker je bila razlika premajhna, da bi pojasnila tako velik odklon. Tisto je bilo usmiljenje in bilo je tvoje. Dve različni stvari si imenovala z istim imenom.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Ne delaj me nedolžne, priča. Malo krivde lahko nosim. Vso krivdo bi prenesla. Nedolžnost pa bi morala pojasnjevati.

**Illuminara**  
Ne delam te ničesar. Pavo bo imel glede prvih enajstih let prav.

Illuminara se je zalotila, da se smehlja umirajoči ženski, ki je zakon uskladila s podlahtjo, in nasmeh skrila. To ni bilo tisto, kar je prostor potreboval. Čudenje je obdržala pod njim, kjer jo je vseeno grelo.

**Illuminara**  
En pogoj. Tega ne bom predložila kot tvojo obrambo. Če bom, bodo slišali odvetnico in imeli bodo prav. Najprej jim povej sama, s svojimi besedami. Številka pride druga, kot nekaj, kar lahko preverijo.

scenes.title: Naj bo resnično
paragraphs: *Sodniška kabina · tretji dan, 23:50*

Vadili sta, dokler niso luči v areni prešle v nočno modrino. Illuminara govora ni napisala. Pod Ketterlyjin hrbet je podložila blazino, kisikovo cevko odmaknila od njenega komolca in poslušala, kako je priznanje prihajalo v vse mehkejših različicah.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Nekaj let sem v interesu reda pri svojih razsodbah uporabljala določeno mero svobode.

**Illuminara**  
Povej tako, kot da bi na tem stolu sedel Pavo.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Enajst let sem goljufala Harrow, ker me je bilo strah.
Kanila je sikala. Ketterly je dlan pritisnila plosko ob naslon stola, kakor da bi hotela stavek zadržati na mestu.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Bolje. Slabše. Kaj od tega?

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da je to prva resnična stvar, ki si jo izrekla nocoj.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Potem naj bo prijazno. Potrebujejo nekaj, s čimer mi bodo lahko odpustili.

**Illuminara**  
Prijazno je bilo to, kar si naredila. Oni pa niso smeli izbrati. Naj bo resnično in naj se sami odločijo, kako prijazni bodo.

Ob dveh zjutraj jo je Ketterly prosila, naj najprej pove računico, naj z njo stopi prednjo. Illuminara je rekla ne, tako nežno, kakor je znala, in namesto tega preostanek noči presedela ob njej. Ko je Ketterly drugič zgrabil kašelj, ji je držala skodelico in ni rekla ničesar. To ni bila rešitev. Bila je edina stvar v stavbi, ki je bila potrebna.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Veš, da si bosta oba želela moj stol, ko me ne bo.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jima morava pustiti nekaj boljšega od stola, za katerega se bosta borila.

scenes.title: Beli dan
paragraphs: *Arena Kessel, odprto klicanje pravila · četrti dan, 14:00*

Klicanje je bilo star običaj: enkrat na leto je vsa arena slišala Sporazum prebran na glas, da nihče ne bi mogel reči, da pravila ni poznal. V njej je sedelo trinajst tisoč ljudi, delegaciji pa sta si stali nasproti v ložah na ledu. Ketterly je govorila zadnja, s svojega stola, s črte, o kateri je odločala devetinštirideset let.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Devetinštirideset let sem tesne razplete odločala tako, da nobena kolonija ni zmagala dvakrat zapored. Prvih enajst let sem to počela iz strahu in Harrowu odvzela cilje, ki so mu pripadali. Devetnajst jih visi na steni v preddverju, z letom in razliko. Ne bom vam govorila, da je bilo prijazno.

Hrup se je začel nizko, kakor voda, ki najde odtok. Iz tretjega obroča je proti stolu priletela čutara. Illuminara je bila med njo in Ketterly, še preden je večina arene videla, da je zapustila roko. Ujela jo je, postavila na led in molčala, ker je trenutek zahteval samo toliko moči.

**Pavo Reisz**  
Če je bila to laž, potem je petdeset let naše vode prišlo iz goljufije in ne bom sedel v areni, zgrajeni na njej.

**Maren Tsoi**  
Podarila nam je naše zmage. Povej naravnost, Pavo. Ti bi temu rekel kraja, mi pa ne.

**Teodor Brask**  
Šesto leto. Zadnja etapa. Ansel Brask je prečkal prvi, za tri desetinke. Moj ded.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Res je. Zmago sem dala Vesperju. Tisto sem naredila njemu.

**Teodor Brask**  
Nikoli več ni drsal.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Vem.
Ni dodala razloga. V tišini, ki je sledila, je mladeničeva jeza ostala natanko tam, kjer je bila, Illuminara pa je opazila, da ji je Ketterly to dovolila.

**Illuminara**  
Dodati moram eno stvar in prosim vas, da ji ne verjamete. V Sporazumu je tabela, ki je niso posodobili od leta 2061. Po mojem izračunu je desetletja izročala tesne razplete Harrowu, Ketterlyjini odkloni pa so ji po mojem izračunu sledili. To je številka, ne obramba. Arhiv, trakovi in popis bodo od nocoj odprti.

**Pavo Reisz**  
In kdo preverja tebe?

**Illuminara**  
Vaši inženirji. Moji bodo sedeli za njimi.

**Pavo Reisz**  
Morda pri Prenosu sploh ne bom sodeloval.

**Illuminara**  
Potem sodeluj pri reviziji. Prostor je manjši, voda pa je od nje odvisna enako.

scenes.title: Štetje
paragraphs: *Prizidek, dvorana B · sedmi dan, 20:30*
Harrowovi inženirji so tabelo našli v štirih urah, njeno napako pa v šestih. Oboje so brez slovesnosti zapisali na tablo.

**Pavo Reisz**  
Preštela si vsa registrirana ognjišča. Dvesto petdeset na naši strani jih je hladnih. Od druge zime v njih ne živi nihče. Prava razlika je dva tisoč sedemsto petdeset, ne tri tisoč. Tvoj odmik je sedem desetink, ne osem.

**Illuminara**  
Sedem. Hvala. Prečrtala bom svojo številko in podpisala vašo.
To je tudi storila, pred vsemi. Številko je spremenilo za desetinko sekunde, prostor pa za precej več.

Nato so inženirji naredili natanko to, kar je od njih zahtevala, in ničesar, česar ni. Harrowova in Vesperjeva ekipa sta vsaka izbrali tri leta, ki jim jih ni nikoli pokazala, štirinajsto, devetindvajseto in štiriinštirideseto, ter izpisali Ketterlyjin zabeleženi odklon in razliko v popisu tistega leta, ne da bi videli delo drugih, dokler ni prišlo na tablo. V štirinajstem in štiriinštiridesetem letu je bil odklon znotraj desetinke indeksiranega dodatka. Devetindvajseto leto je bilo nerodno: Ketterly je odklonila štiri desetinke manj, kakor je napovedovala razlika, in nihče ni znal povedati zakaj. Ostanek so pustili na tabli nepojasnjen.

Preizkusili so tudi tekmujočo razlago, da je preprosto izmenjevala zmagovalce in je stopnišče le naključje. Izmenjevanje bi cilj odklonilo šele po dveh zmagah ene kolonije. Odkloni so se pojavljali tudi v letih brez takšne zgodovine in rasli skupaj s popisom, ne glede na to, katera kolonija je zmagala nazadnje.

**Pavo Reisz**  
Prav. Trend je. Zaradi tega še ni pošten.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Zaradi tega sta dve stvari. Enajst let je izbrala stran. Osemintrideset let je sledila tabeli, ki ni več govorila resnice.

Do polnoči sta bila na tabli dva predloga. Harrowov glavni inženir je hotel, da se dodatek indeksira po popisu, ki bi ga obe koloniji vsako leto skupaj ponovili, brez človeške roke v njem. Maren je hotela zapisati v Sporazum to, kar je Ketterly delala ročno: natisnjeni dodatek za menjavo v višini treh desetink sekunde za kolonijo, ki je izgubila prejšnje leto.

**Pavo Reisz**  
To je miloščina v plašču pravila.

**Maren Tsoi**  
Na tem smo že živeli. Tako lahko vsaj kdo glasuje proti.

**Illuminara**  
Prav to je bistvo. Popis popravi napako. Dodatek za menjavo dobroto naredi javno, o javni dobroti pa se je mogoče prepirati, jo skrajšati, končati. Ketterlyjini se je lahko samo verjelo ali ne.

Sporazum je vsaki delegaciji dovoljeval, da svojo kolonijo zaveže z lastno večino, zato sta glasovali ločeno. Popisna tabela je v obeh delegacijah minila brez glasu proti. Dodatek za menjavo je pri Vesperju minil z osmimi glasovi proti enemu, pri Harrowu pa s petimi proti štirim; Pavo je bil med štirimi. Po desetem Prenosu bi prenehal veljati, če ga obe delegaciji ne bi ponovno potrdili, vsaka kolonija pa bi podaljšanje lahko zavrnila brez kazni ali izgube položaja. Pavo je zahteval, da se njegov ne zapiše ob pravilu, ne pod njim, in tako je bilo.

**Teodor Brask**  
Drsal bom. Nisem ji odpustil.

**Illuminara**  
Nihče te ni prosil.
Nato je izpostavila točko, ki je ni nihče napisal na tablo.

**Illuminara**  
Prvih enajst let ni moje poravnati, pa tudi koloniji ju ne moreta. Pripadajo ljudem, ki so izgubili tiste cilje.

Bralca, ki bi stala ob ciljni črti, sta dobila nalogo ponovno prebrati trakove prvih enajstih let. Kjer bi trak, ne roka, pokazal, da je prvi Harrow, bi se evidenca spremenila v imenu drsalca in z datumom. Drsalec ali družina bi izbrala popravljeni izid, zmanjšanje Vesperjevega odvzema za eno sezono v dobro gospodinjstva, oboje ali nič. Maren je rekla, da bo Vesper plačal vsakomur, ki bo zahteval.

**Teodor Brask**  
Vrnite Anselovo ime. Vodo obdržite.
Na galeriji so se drsalci, ki so v zadnjem desetletju zmagali v tesnih ciljih, tiho prepirali, katera od njihovih medalj ima zdaj zvezdico. Nihče jim ni rekel, da jih to ne bi smelo motiti.
Ob zori je vodni dnevnik pristal na odprti tabli: vsak zapis črpalke iz obeh kolonij, ki sta ga odtlej obe brali, mesec za mesecem.

scenes.title: Trak
paragraphs: *Arena Kessel, ciljna črta · deseti dan, Prenos, 15:20*

Zadnja etapa je bila tako tesna, da je trinajst tisoč ljudi hkrati prenehalo dihati. Harrowov zadnji drsalec je prečkal prvi za šest desetink sekunde in po stari črki pravila bi bilo s tem konec: Harrow za dve desetinki, razsodila pa bi tabela, ki je nihče ni prebral od leta 2061.

Nihče ni razsodil. Trak se je prikazal na tabli z novim dodatkom in dodatkom za menjavo ob njem, poraženec prejšnjega leta je bil Harrow, ob črti pa sta stala dva bralca, po eden iz vsake lože, in ga prebrala naglas. Maren je prebrala računico. Pavo je, ker je pravilo določalo, da poraženi delegat prebere razliko, prebral zadnjo vrstico, čeprav je glasoval proti pravilu, ki mu jo je dalo.

**Pavo Reisz**  
Surovi cilj, Harrow za šest desetink. Indeksirani dodatek Vesperju, ena cela ena. Dodatek za menjavo Harrowu, tri desetinke. Končni izid: Vesper za dve desetinki.

Glas mu je zdržal. Z Vesperjevih tribun se je dvignil zvok, ki ni bil povsem veselje, ker so zdaj vedeli, iz česa so bile narejene njihove zmage, in zvenel je kakor ljudje, ki dobivajo nazaj nekaj, kar jim je že od nekdaj napol pripadalo. Na Harrowovi strani ni nihče ničesar vrgel. Teodor Brask, ki je brez napake oddrsal drugo etapo, je stal z rokami na kolenih in dolgo gledal tablo. Ni ploskal. Ni odšel.
Ketterly je gledala s starega stola. Nihče ji ni dal zastavice v roko. Imela je kanilo in skodelico čaja, iz katere ni pila, in prvič v devetinštiridesetih letih ji ni bilo treba o ničemer odločiti.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Osem desetink, kajne?

**Illuminara**  
Sedem.

**Ketterly Osa**  
Sedem. Popravil Harrowov inženir, javno. Zdaj lahko umrem.

Umrla je naslednji četrtek, v spanju, s trakom, pripetim nad posteljo, in odprtim ventilom. Pavo Reisz je prišel na pogreb in stal zadaj. Illuminari je povedal, da prvih enajstih let ni odpustil in da je prišel zaradi drugih osemintridesetih. Stol je ostal privit v tla kabine. Naslednjo sezono sta na njem sedela dva človeka, po eden iz vsake kolonije, in nobeden ni mogel nagniti črte.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara je spoznala, da Ketterlyjina skrivna dobrota skriva dve različni zgodovini: ukradenih prvih enajst let in osemintrideset let nezavednega popravljanja zamrznjenega pravila; ker dokazov ni hotela spremeniti v oprostitev, je obema kolonijama pomagala preveriti resnico, prizadetim prepustiti izbiro lastnega povračila ter eno skrito roko nadomestiti z javnim pravilom, ki so ga lahko sprejeli, mu ugovarjali in ga pozneje končali.
